To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

contemporaneous text can be effectively used as side-information in language modeling, and that the effectiveness of this approach depends on the amount of available side-corpus and the similarity between the side-corpus and documents being processed.

(1) contemporaneous text can be used as side-information for improving language models for speech recognition, (2) contemporaneous text is most useful for languages with limited training material, (3) contemporaneous text from a language with rich linguistic resources can be used for improving a language model in a language with limited resources, and (4) contemporaneous text need not be a direct translation of the target language document to be processed, but can be independent text from the same domain and time period.

(1) contemporaneous text from a language with abundant resources can be used to improve language modeling of a language with scarce resources, and (2) the amount of Chinese text available for training the language model does not have to be large.

how one can exploit contemporaneous text in a resource-rich language (e.g., English) to improve statistical language models for processing documents in a resource-scarce language (e.g. Chinese).
